extracted.intended_audience: authors, reviewers, and editors of health economic evaluations; health economists and HTA analysts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reporting economic evaluations of health interventions so that readers, reviewers, and decision makers can interpret, use, and (where appropriate) replicate studies. This covers title/abstract, methods, costs/benefits classification, perspective, transparency, equity, stakeholder involvement, and context-specific issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the 28-item CHEERS 2022 checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: CHEERS 2022 includes a 28-item checklist that outlines how and when these reporting standards should be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The checklist is the consolidated reporting standard for health economic evaluations (see online checklist and downloadable .doc). It is designed to improve reporting and transparency rather than to assess methodological quality or be used as a quantitative scoring tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and abstract reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Include appropriate information in the title and abstract to aid those researching economic evaluation literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some checklist items (e.g., title, abstract) were included specifically to aid literature searching and identification; ensure these fields clearly convey that the study is an economic evaluation and summarize the comparisons, perspective, and key results.

rubrics_metrics.name: State what interventions are being compared and the context
rubrics_metrics.description: Report which health interventions (or courses of action) are being compared and the context in which the evaluation is conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide enough detail on comparators and setting so readers and decision makers can understand applicability and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe how the evaluation was undertaken (methods transparency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly describe the methods used to conduct the economic evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include design, modelling approaches, data sources, analytic methods, assumptions, and any deviations from protocol so readers can appraise and replicate the analysis where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report findings and details to aid interpretation and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Present results and key details that allow readers to interpret findings and consider their use in decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report outcomes, costs, incremental analyses, uncertainty, and interpretation with sufficient context for policy makers, payers, clinicians, and other stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide sufficient information to enable replication
rubrics_metrics.description: Report study elements in enough detail to allow other researchers to reproduce or replicate the analysis where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes data sources, model structure, parameter values, assumptions, and (where applicable) access to model code or datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use CHEERS as a method quality assessment or quantitative score
rubrics_metrics.description: CHEERS is reporting guidance and should not be inappropriately used to assess the quality of methods or to produce quantitative scores in systematic reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors note past misuse: CHEERS was designed to evaluate reporting completeness, not methodological rigor or to be used as a scoring instrument for study quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include reporting guidance for cost–benefit analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Address the previous absence of reporting guidance on cost–benefit analyses by including appropriate reporting items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CHEERS 2022 expands scope to cover cost–benefit analyses in addition to cost-effectiveness/cost-utility frameworks; follow checklist items relevant to cost–benefit format.

rubrics_metrics.name: State and justify the perspective of the economic evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the perspective adopted for the evaluation (e.g., healthcare sector, societal) and justify that choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updates reflect Second Panel recommendations; perspective affects which costs and consequences are included and should be explicitly described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classify costs and benefits in a structured table
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a structured classification of costs and benefits (e.g., in a table) to clarify what is included and excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using a structured table improves clarity and comparability across studies by explicitly listing categories of costs/benefits and their treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report inclusion/exclusion of related and unrelated healthcare costs in added years of life
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly report whether related and unrelated healthcare costs in added years of life are included and how they were handled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflects methodological updates (Second Panel) — explicitly state treatment of future healthcare costs in survival gains to allow appropriate interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-specify and report health economic analysis plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and report health economic analysis plans (HEAPs) to document planned analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The update highlights increasing calls for HEAPs; reporting should indicate whether a plan existed, where it can be accessed, and any departures from it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model transparency and open-source models/data sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Report on model accessibility, openness, and data sharing to support scrutiny and reuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CHEERS 2022 recognizes the use of open-source models and growing journal data-sharing policies; authors should provide information on model code, calibration, and how to access materials where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report consequences beyond health outcomes (equity and distributional effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: When analyses attempt to capture consequences beyond health (e.g., equity, distributional effects), report these explicitly and describe methods used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Growing interest in equity means reporting should state which distributional/ equity impacts were considered and how they were measured or modelled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe stakeholder participation (including patients and public)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the extent and nature of stakeholder involvement in study design, conduct, or dissemination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CHEERS 2022 emphasizes stakeholder participation; describe who was involved (patients, public, clinicians, payers), their role, and how their input influenced the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for context-specific issues (immunization, global health, LMICs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Address reporting elements relevant to immunization programs, global health interventions, and evaluations in low- and middle-income countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CHEERS 2022 includes consideration of methods and reporting needed for policy decisions in immunization and LMIC contexts — report context-specific assumptions, data, and transferability considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signpost and use CHEERS resources (full report, explanation and elaboration, patient guide, checklist, videos)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the full CHEERS 2022 Explanation & Elaboration report and companion materials to inform reporting and interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report provides rationale, supporting evidence, examples, and explanations for each checklist item; authors and reviewers should consult these companion resources for detailed guidance and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of CHEERS-AI and methodological extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Note related extensions (e.g., CHEERS-AI) and specialized guidance that may apply to particular methods or technologies used in economic evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ISPOR page lists CHEERS-AI and other resources — consult these when analyses involve AI-derived models or other emerging methods with additional reporting needs.
